title: perf(canary): enhanced auto-detection for latency/throughput regressions with rollout guards
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: The existing perf-canary pipeline detects regressions using fixed thresholds and simple window comparisons. This PR improves automated detection accuracy for small-but-significant latency and throughput regressions, reduces false positives during traffic churn, and integrates automatic rollout guards with the rollout engine. Key changes: 1) Statistical detection: introduce an EWMA + bootstrapped confidence interval detector for p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec throughput to detect small regressions with configurable sensitivity; 2) Baseline selection: automatic baseline selection by traffic-weighted sampling and model-variant affinity to avoid noisy baselines during feature rollouts; 3) Multi-metric scoring: aggregate latency/throughput/error delta into a single regression score with tunable weights and hysteresis; 4) Rollout guards: new controller hooks that will automatically pause or rollback canaries when score exceeds threshold, with built-in cooldown and operator override; 5) Observability: new dashboards, per-canary traces, and alerting rules; 6) CI: add a perf-canary-e2e check to run on release candidates. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and Linear tickets linked (ENG-6123, ENG-6199) - [x] Implementation of detector + unit tests - [x] Integration with rollout controller + e2e tests - [x] Dashboards and runbook updates - [x] Documentation and console UI annotations Backwards compatibility: default sensitivity uses current thresholds so existing canaries behave the same unless teams opt into the enhanced detector. Configuration: teams can opt into the new detector via canary.policy.detection = "enhanced" and tune sensitivity via canary.policy.detection.sensitivity = "low|medium|high". Release notes: see release_notes field below.

review_comments: Benji Coleman (review): Overall looks good. Two questions: 1) Have you run the detector under noisy load patterns (startup spikes)? 2) Can we avoid bootstrapping on every evaluation to reduce cost?

Aisha Kapoor (reply): Good points. I added a traffic-weighted baseline cache and only bootstrap on first evaluation or if baseline TTL expired. Added tests for spike scenarios using the synthetic workload harness.
Marissa Lee (review): Please add a note in the runbook about operator overrides and the expected SLO if a canary is paused automatically.
Aisha Kapoor (reply): Added runbook section and console hint that surfaces the override token and cooldown period.
David Ortiz (LGTM): Verified e2e in staging, checked dashboards and rollback behavior. Approving.

release_notes: Enhancement: Improved automatic detection for canary performance regressions using EWMA + bootstrapped confidence intervals for latency and throughput.
New: Automatic rollout guards that can pause or rollback canaries when multi-metric regression score exceeds configurable thresholds.
Docs: runbook and tuning guide added; console now surfaces guard actions and operator override controls.
Backward compatibility: Default detection mode remains unchanged; teams must opt into the enhanced detector via canary.policy.detection.
